entities.summary:
Ptahmose was a High Priest of Amun and Vizier of southern Egypt-(Upper Egypt), under Amenhotep III. 

As Vizier, Ptahmose played a crucial role in the administration of Egypt during the reign of Amenhotep III, who ruled from 1390 to 1362 BCE. Ptahmose's tenure as Vizier is believed to have begun during the early part of Amenhotep III's reign, with some historians placing it as early as 1398 BC, while others suggest it may have started as late as 1378 BC. 

Ptahmose's significance extends beyond his administrative duties, as he was also a key figure in the religious and cultural life of ancient Egypt. As High Priest of Amun, Ptahmose oversaw the construction of several temples and monuments, including the temple of Amun at Karnak, which was one of the largest and most important temples in Egypt. 

Ptahmose's legacy can be seen in the many architectural and artistic achievements of the New Kingdom period, which he helped to shape through his religious and cultural policies. His influence can be seen in the many temples, tombs, and monuments that were built during his reign, which reflect the high level of artistic and architectural achievement of ancient Egypt during this period. 

Ptahmose's impact on the history of Egypt is still felt today, as his legacy continues to inspire wonder and awe in visitors to the temples and monuments that he helped to create.
